subject: Reserved pool scale-up proposal — 8→16 GPUs, updated monthly commit & SLA
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@neuralscale.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neuralscale.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — interested in expanding reserved pool to 16 GPUs

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the Q2 review call — NeuralScale’s usage has grown faster than we forecasted. Attached is our Q2 usage export showing a 2.4x increase in peak token throughput and sustained inference jobs.

We’re evaluating options for the upcoming renewal and want to move from an 8 GPU reserved pool to a 16 GPU pool for the next 12 months. Key asks from our side:
- Monthly commit to reflect the higher baseline (please propose updated pricing tiers).
- A throughput guarantee for 90th percentile token latency under our common workload (we can provide sample traffic patterns).
- Staged activation: we’d like a 2-week canary then full ramp within one month.

Can you share a proposal with pricing, activation timeline, and any SLA changes? Procurement is looped (procurement@neuralscale.ai) — they’ll want billing cadence and contract term language.

Attachments: NeuralScale_Usage_Q2_2026.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Olivia Chen
Account Executive, NeuralScale
olivia@neuralscale.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@neuralscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — interested in expanding reserved pool to 16 GPUs

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the usage file. This is great context.

High-level response and next steps from our side:
1) We can support a move to 16 GPUs and propose two commercial options: a flat monthly commit with volume discount vs. a staged ramp (8→12→16) with blended pricing. I’ll ask Marissa to share the draft numbers.
2) For throughput SLAs we typically publish baseline 95th/90th latency targets tied to the committed pool and sequence-length percentiles. Karthik, can you review the sample traffic and surface realistic 90th percentile latency guarantees and any guardrails (burst queueing, backfill behavior)?
3) Staged activation is straightforward: ops runbook, a 2-week canary (single region), then cross-region activation. Grace, please attach the staged activation runbook draft and estimate ops hours.

I’ll consolidate the commercial terms and a proposed activation schedule by early next week so procurement has something to review.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@neuralscale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed terms for 16 GPU reserved pool (draft)

Hi Olivia / team — looping in a draft commercial proposal and the ops runbook. Key items in this draft (see Redwood_ReservedPool_Proposal_v3.pdf):

Commercial options (summary):
- Option A (single-step): 16 GPU monthly commit — list price $X/month, committed discount applied; 12-month term; 30-day billing cadence.
- Option B (phased ramp): Start at 8 GPUs month 1, 12 GPUs month 2, 16 GPUs month 3 onward — blended pricing to smooth cashflow.

SLA / throughput notes:
- We can commit a 90th percentile token-latency SLA for the referenced traffic envelope. SLA requires a minimum commit (Option A qualifies; Option B will have conditional guarantees during ramp).
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a compatible lower-precision variant if capacity is constrained; notifications and credits defined in Section 4.

Operational plan:
- Canary: 14 days in us-west-2 (single AZ) with canary runway for model variants.
- Full activation target: up to 30 days after signed amendment depending on capacity lead time.
- Ops estimate: ~48 engineer-hours for activation and validation (see StagedActivation_Runbook.md).

Attachments: Redwood_ReservedPool_Proposal_v3.pdf (pdf), StagedActivation_Runbook.md (md)

Olivia — I put numbers in the PDF. If procurement needs a net-30 invoice or purchase-order flow, let us know and we’ll align on contract language.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Markus Bauer <markus.bauer@neuralscale.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@neuralscale.ai>
Cc: procurement@neuralscale.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed terms for 16 GPU reserved pool (draft)

Thanks — this looks promising. A few clarifying questions from engineering and procurement:

Engineering:
- Can you publish the 90th percentile latency numbers using our provided sample traces (Olivia attached in the original spreadsheet)? We need the numbers broken out by sequence length buckets (<=512, 513–2048, >2048).
- For the staged activation, can you confirm rollback thresholds and expected mean-time-to-failover if a canary detects regressions?

Procurement:
- Preferred payment: Net 30 via ACH. Please confirm invoice cadence.
- We’ll need the amendment language for the monthly commit and an executed DocuSign by July 22 to hit our internal budget cycle.

Can you also confirm whether there’s any upfront on-boarding fee for the staged activation?

Thanks —
Markus Bauer
CTO, NeuralScale
markus.bauer@neuralscale.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Markus Bauer <markus.bauer@neuralscale.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@neuralscale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, procurement@neuralscale.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed terms for 16 GPU reserved pool (draft)

Markus / team — quick summary and proposed next steps.

Summary of what we agreed to in the draft:
- Commercial: Option A (16 GPU monthly commit) chosen by NeuralScale. 12-month term, Net-30 invoicing. Final prices in Redwood_ReservedPool_Proposal_v3.pdf.
- SLA: Redwood will provide per-sequence-length 90th percentile latency targets for the workload you supplied (we’ll publish the numbers in an addendum). Credits for SLA misses will be defined in the amendment.
- Activation: 14-day canary in us-west-2, rollback thresholds: >15% regression in 90th latency or >5% error-rate increase triggers immediate rollback and incident postmortem. Mean-time-to-failover: target <30 minutes.
- Onboarding fees: waived for this renewal as a commercial concession.

Next steps / timing:
1) Marissa: share final PDF with redlined amendment for signature. (Marissa — can you push DocuSign link by EOD 7/12?)
2) Karthik & engineering: finalize the per-bucket 90th latency numbers and upload addendum by 7/15.
3) NeuralScale procurement: execute DocuSign by 7/22 to meet your budget cycle.
4) Ops (Grace): schedule activation window; target canary start 7/29 with full ramp by 8/12 pending validation.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/doc/RED-NS-2026-001
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
Runbook (ops): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/staged-activation-runbook

If that all looks good I’ll mark the deal stage to "Ready for Signature" and coordinate the activation calendar.

Thanks everyone —
Priyom
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com
